correctness.rationale: Every proper tube is a mixed subset and two disjoint mixed tubes force a directed 2-cycle; hence proper tubings are exactly strict mixed-subset chains. In a dimension n-2 simple polytope, two-faces are precisely (n-4)-tube chains. Two omitted nonadjacent ranks always allow 2x2=4 completions (including the initial rank-2 boundary), adjacent noninitial ranks allow 3!=6, and ranks 2 and 3 omitted allow 2ab=6 or 8 completions according to a+b=4. Exhaustive double-counting yields each displayed multiplicity. The type-A root-plane argument bounds generalized-permutohedron two-faces by 6 sides. Exact standalone finite checker passed 25 ordered (p,q) instances through n=8 and 216147 2-face groups; finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Galashin proves the face poset and Sack gives h- and f-enumeration for the very same poset family, so these ingredients are not novel. Their results as inspected do not state polygon-type counts. The new claim is an all-size complete 4/6/8-gon classification and the exact octagon multiplicity, which is not implied by the h-vector alone: for three possible polygon types, f_2 and total vertex-face incidence give only two linear constraints. An older different poset-associahedron construction includes isolated octagon examples; octagon occurrence per se is not claimed new. Targeted published-paper, published-finding corpus, and historical-claim checks revealed no covering exact refinement. Risk remains of an unindexed equivalent local-face enumeration.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently termed local rank-gap enumerations could coincide with this exact polygon-type formula.
The 2015 same-named older poset family has octagons, so novelty excludes discovery of octagons in general.

value.rationale: The complete polygon-type spectrum is a natural local invariant of a canonical two-parameter family; it distinguishes Galashin poset associahedra from generalized permutohedra by an exact positive octagon count for every p,q>=2, and refines known f/h-vector data whose constraints alone do not determine octagon frequency. A complete all-size local face classification, rather than a single unmotivated example, has natural geometric relevance to boundary combinatorics and related polytope classes.
